header.name: Analytic Number Theory
header.description: Analytic Number Theory is a branch of mathematics that uses analytic tools to solve number theoritic problems. It is well-known for its results on prime numbers (Prime Number Theorem and Riemann Zeta function). In this course the main aim is to study the Riemann Zeta function and its connection with the distribution of prime numbers and finally to prove the Prime Number Theorem - PNT using analytic tools.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Student will learn about Riemann zeta function and its connection with Prime Number Theorem- PNT.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine mean values of arithmetic functions using different methods.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine the distribution of primes and different versions of PNT.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate the use of properties of Riemann Zeta function in the proof of the PNT and its consequences.

lecture_topics: Introduction to: Riemann Zeta function and Prime Number Theorem
Arithmetic Functions I : Additive and Multiplicative functions
The Von Mangoldt function and Divisor function
Arithmetic Functions II : Euler's summation formula
Distribution of Primes I : Chebyshev's type estimate
The PNT and averages of Moebius function
Arithmetic Functions III : Analytic and Algebraic properties of Dirichlet series
Mellin transform representation of Dirichlet series
Analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function
Lower bounds for error terms in summatory functions
Distribution of Primes II : Upper and Lower bounds of Riemann Zeta function
Proof of the PNT and its consequences
